- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 78–80 range), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “rebound” or “mean reversion” effect.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day forecast, suggesting it underestimates downward momentum or fails to account for seasonal/structural decline.
- Model often fails to adjust for recent strong upward trends — e.g., if history shows 75–80, model still forecasts 70–75, ignoring momentum.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections after peaks — e.g., after 80, model predicts 70–75, but true drops to 60–65.
- Model shows lagged response to recent price changes — e.g., if price drops 5 days ago, model doesn’t immediately reflect it in forecast.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates sharp drops and overestimates gradual declines.
- Model often overcorrects after a sharp drop — e.g., after 60, model forecasts 70–75, but true rebounds to 65–70, then drops again.
- Model fails to account for “tail risk” — underestimates extreme downward moves (e.g., 50–55 range) after 70–75.
- Model exhibits “memory decay” — recent history (last 5–7 days) is underweighted in forecasting, leading to persistent bias.
